articles.title: Burnham criticised for EV and North Sea drilling approach as wildfires heighten climate fears
articles.description:
Reduction in EV sales targets could add millions of tonnes of CO2 to emissions as UK faces impact of global heating

Andy Burnham has been criticised for moving to cut electric vehicle (EV) sales targets and accept North Sea drilling at a time of devastating wildfires caused by the climate emergency.

The prime minister for the first time acknowledged on Friday that the climate crisis was behind hundreds of wildfires that have ripped across the parts of the UK.

articles.title: ‘It’s due to climate’: the people of Stourbridge on the town’s wildfires
articles.description:
Thursday has been described by residents as ‘horrendous’, ‘distressing’ and ‘one of the scariest days of my life’

People in Stourbridge have described the fires that devastated more than a dozen homes as “horrendous” and “distressing”, with one describing blazes that surpassed the height of residential houses.

Multiple fires spread across the West Midlands on Thursday as temperatures reached record highs of 38.1C in the UK, during the country’s fifth consecutive heatwave.

articles.title: One dead, dozens injured and thousands evacuated in Croatian wildfires – as it happened
articles.description:
Firefighters discover body and say more than 40 people hurt in the Lokva Rogoznica and Omiš areas

England has received just 4mm of rain so far in August, or 6% of the long-term average for the month, the Environment Agency said on Friday, as reported by PA.

It follows the driest July on record for the country, when only 7mm of rain was measured, or 10% of the average.

articles.title: Indonesia wildfires threaten orangutans rescued from animal traffickers
articles.description:
Blaze fuelled by hot, dry and windy conditions comes within metres of West Kalimantan rehabilitation centre

Orangutans rescued from wildlife traffickers face a new threat from the record number of fires that have broken out in Indonesia in recent weeks.

Flames have come within metres of an animal rehabilitation centre in West Kalimantan as hot, dry and windy conditions have been amplified by a powerful El Niño and the human-driven climate crisis.

articles.title: ‘The colander worked best!’ Guardian readers share their experience of the solar eclipse
articles.description:
Readers recall the breathtaking sight and community spirit of the rare celestial treat – and the handmade contraptions they saw it through

On Wednesday evening, millions of people in Europe watched a rare solar eclipse. We asked some of them to share their photographs and experiences of this celestial treat.

Here are some of their responses.

articles.title: Trump administration pulls support for annual Arctic environmental report
articles.description:
Move by National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration is latest government rollback of climate science activity

The Trump administration has pulled its support for an annual report on the environmental changes across the Arctic, a region that is already heating up four times faster than the global average due to the climate crisis.

On Tuesday, Kim Doster, the communications director of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa), said the federal agency was withdrawing its support for the Arctic Report Card, which has provided environmental updates on the region to scientists and the public since 2006.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Burnham to consider ban on disposable barbecues as wildfires rage in UK
articles.description:
PM to look at imposing restriction on devices in public spaces, though campaigners fear it does not go far enough

The government will look at banning disposable barbecues as wildfires continue to rage across the UK, Andy Burnham has said.

Disposable barbecues have been the cause of a number of serious fires over the last few years, but campaigners were critical of the prime minister’s failure to link those fires more broadly to the climate crisis.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Halting the march of the African armyworm: a natural cure offers hope to farmers
articles.description:
South African scientist’s breakthrough research shows soil fungus could be used in fight against devastating crop pest

Hearing about fields full of dead caterpillars enveloped in a mysterious white substance intrigued the South African scientist Letodi Luki Mathulwe. Something was killing off the African armyworm – one of the most devastating pests for farmers in east and southern Africa.

The white substance was a naturally occurring fungus and it was wiping out the caterpillar, which gained its name from its march-like advance through fields of crops.

articles.title: All-British chocolate bar made by scientists using Reading-grown cocoa
articles.description:
Master’s student made first bar with 100% UK ingredients since 1932 to highlight affect of climate crisis on cocoa plants

The late queen was the only person in history to have ever eaten a chocolate bar made with 100% British ingredients, after she was given one as a six-year-old in 1932 by the confectioner Rowntree’s.

The bar was created from a glasshouse-grown cocoa plant, at Rowntree’s headquarters in York.

articles.title: Burnham faces mass call from police chiefs to block early release of PC Harper’s killers
articles.description:
Letter signed by 50 police leaders, including every chief constable in England and Wales, says there is ‘profound strength of feeling across policing’

Andy Burnham is facing an unprecedented mass call from police chiefs to block the early release of PC Andrew Harper’s killers, as unions warned his emergency plan to create more space in prisons risked causing confusion or prisoners being freed by mistake.

A letter signed by 50 police leaders across the UK, including every chief constable in England and Wales, called on the prime minister to do everything in his power to stop the killers benefiting from a programme designed to free up prison spaces, saying there was “a profound strength of feeling across policing” that this should not happen.

Continue reading...
